Filtering rows by `updated_at >= promoted_container_started_at` and accepting any positive `attempt_count` can still false-pass: a row may already have historical attempts, and a heartbeat updates `updated_at` without incrementing `attempt_count`. For a worker promotion gate, capture a validated per-job `(id, attempt_count)` baseline before promotion, force recreation of the fixed-name worker container, verify the promoted container ID changed and its image revision label equals the requested immutable SHA, then accept only a row updated after the promoted start time whose current attempt count is strictly greater than that job's pre-promotion count. This combination preserves immediate new-container claims, excludes pre-start old-container claims, and prevents a heartbeat on a historically attempted row from counting as a new release attempt. Also enforce any configurable queue wait as an integer strictly greater than the 120-second lease; a safe default alone is not an invariant when operators can override it downward.


### Forced recreation requires validating rollback state before mutation

When promotion uses `docker compose up --force-recreate`, validate the persisted previous image tag before replacing the usable container. A state-file value must be exactly the expected immutable tag format (for this workflow, one lowercase 40-hex Git SHA, which also rejects embedded newlines/env-file injection), and `docker image inspect` must confirm the corresponding rollback image exists locally with the same OCI revision label. Fail before mutation if either check fails. Otherwise a corrupt state file or missing rollback image is discovered only after destructive recreation, when automated rollback can no longer restore the previous worker.


### Immutable-tag validation must be symmetric

If rollback state is constrained to an immutable 40-hex commit SHA, apply the identical validation to the incoming deployment tag before loading images or mutating containers. Otherwise a mutable incoming tag such as `latest` can deploy successfully and be persisted, then poison the next deployment because the same value is rejected when read as rollback state. Validate both incoming and stored tags against the same invariant and assert both checks in deployment validation.


### Correction: take the attempt baseline after old-worker termination, before new-worker start

A pre-promotion per-job attempt baseline plus a promoted `StartedAt` filter still leaves a theoretical attribution race: the old worker can claim after the baseline and update around shutdown. Use a two-phase Compose handoff instead. Run `docker compose up --no-start --force-recreate` so the fixed-name old container is stopped/removed and the promoted container is created but not running; validate the new container ID/revision; then capture the per-job attempt baseline while no meeting worker is running; finally `docker compose start clover-meeting-worker`. Compare post-start attempts to that quiescent baseline. This creates a provable old-worker-free boundary while preserving claims made immediately after new-worker startup. Keep rollback trapped across both phases.


### Prefer exact-container claim evidence over shared queue timestamps

Even a quiescent per-job database baseline cannot identify which worker incremented an attempt if another worker for the same tenant exists, and comparing Docker host `StartedAt` with PostgreSQL `updated_at` assumes synchronized clocks. A stronger deployment gate is a bounded claim marker emitted immediately after `Queue.Claim`, containing only non-secret job metadata, then read via `docker logs` from the exact prepared/promoted container ID whose immutable revision was verified. Because the container was newly created with `--no-start --force-recreate`, its entire log stream belongs to that release; no timestamp filter or database clock comparison is required, and an immediate pre-readiness claim remains visible. Treat Docker log-read failures as distinct fail-closed errors. Keep the >lease timeout because an abandoned running job may not become claimable until its prior lease expires.


### Docker `running` is not application readiness; use exact-container ready and structured claim markers

A container enters Docker `running` state while its shell startup preflight may still be executing. For a worker with no HTTP health endpoint, emit a fixed application-ready log marker only after dependencies/configuration and worker construction succeed, and require that marker from the exact prepared container ID before accepting readiness. Revalidate container ID, running state, restart count, and ready marker again immediately before persisting the verified release state. For claim evidence, do not accept a bare prefix: parse a complete UUID following the fixed claim marker and reject the nil UUID. Add a boundary test proving the claim marker is already present when `Prepare` begins, not merely after `ProcessOne` finishes.


### Ready markers must follow active dependency authentication, not lazy client construction

`pgxpool.NewWithConfig` creates a lazy pool and can succeed with invalid credentials; a TCP-only Compose preflight also proves only that PostgreSQL is listening. Before emitting a worker application-ready marker, explicitly `Ping` the pool under the startup timeout and fail closed on authentication/connectivity errors. Readiness evidence is only meaningful after active dependency checks, especially when tenant policy is paused or the queue is empty and no claim marker will be required during deployment.


### Deployment evidence cannot compensate for an unscoped multi-tenant claim query

If a standalone worker is configured with `CLOVEROPS_ORGANIZATION_ID`, its queue claim API must require that organization and include `organization_id = ...` in the candidate query. Scoping only deployment baselines/policy reads is insufficient: the promoted worker could claim another tenant's job, emit valid exact-container claim evidence, and falsely satisfy the target tenant's rollout gate while also processing data outside its configured scope. Bind the worker store to its parsed non-nil organization ID and add an integration fixture where an earlier eligible job from another tenant is skipped.

## TIL: serialize CloverOps full-module integration tests that share one temporary PostgreSQL database

When `CLOVEROPS_TEST_DATABASE_URL` points every CloverOps package at the same temporary PostgreSQL database, plain `GOWORK=off go test ./...` may run packages concurrently and make independent migration fixtures contend on the same database. Observed symptoms include duplicate `pg_extension_name_index` rows and deadlocks while applying `migrations/014_meeting_intelligence.sql`; these are test-environment collisions, not evidence that an affected package's focused tests failed.

For release validation, start a fresh disposable PostgreSQL container and run the full backend suite serially with `GOWORK=off go test -p 1 ./... -count=1`. Keep focused affected-package tests and `-race` tests as separate gates. Do not reuse a database contaminated by a prior concurrent full-suite run.



## Meeting worker restart recovery: a stage digest is not stage output

CloverOps `meeting_panel_stages.output_digest` proves what output was previously persisted/observed, but it cannot reconstruct the specialist output bytes. `Prepare` may therefore restore a completed stage with a digest and an empty in-memory `StageResult.Output`. Never pass that hash-only receipt to the judge as if it were the specialist result. Under the current store API, rerun a completed specialist when its output bytes are unavailable, then re-verify its durable side effects; alternatively, introduce an explicit bounded typed result store/loader. Durable finding existence alone does not reconstruct the judge input.



## Durable specialist receipts must identify committed findings, not count tool attempts

For restartable CloverOps meeting stages, Swarm `tool_calls_by_name` is invocation telemetry: it includes failed calls and idempotent retries, so its count cannot be equated with unique committed `meeting_findings` rows. Require each specialist's bounded final receipt to list the stable finding IDs it considers committed, validate that receipt strictly (bounded, unique IDs), and verify the exact stage/category-scoped durable ID set under the active lease. On a specialist rerun, isolate or replace that stage's prior findings before new submissions so a changed deterministic set cannot leave an unrecoverable union of old and new rows. If a valid durable verdict already exists after restart, verify and complete that terminal workflow before rerunning or clearing any specialist stage; a committed verdict makes the panel immutable. Bound every durable verification/reset operation by the stage timeout and preserve separate retry/error classes for verification, malformed receipts, lease loss, and runner failures.



## Aggregate human review must dominate action materialization

In the CloverOps meeting verdict path, a finding's six policy predicates can be individually eligible while the aggregate verdict still requires human review because another finding is ineligible or explicitly `needs_review`. Never materialize such an accepted action as `automatic/automatic`: aggregate `review.required=true` must force every materialized action decision to `auto_create_eligible=false`, `decision_type=human`, and `status=pending`. The judge submission boundary may create only `pending` human review; it must not accept `approved`, `changes_requested`, or `rejected` as if the model were an authenticated human reviewer. Keep those later transitions behind a separate authenticated human operation.



## Meeting mutation capabilities must bind to the exact active lease attempt

A run/job-scoped signed MCP capability is insufficient for meeting finding or verdict mutations when queue jobs can be reclaimed. An assertion from expired lease A can remain cryptographically valid after lease B claims the same job; checking only `status='running'`, a non-null lease token, and lease expiry lets the stale agent mutate under B's authority. Include the exact queue `lease_token` (or an equivalent unguessable attempt nonce) in the signed meeting capability, propagate it through the worker panel request and MCP context, and require exact equality with `meeting_ingest_jobs.lease_token` in every finding/verdict mutation transaction. Keep read tools run/job-scoped if intended, but mutation authorization must fail closed for a stale attempt. Regression coverage should claim with lease A, replace it with lease B, and prove A is rejected for both finding and verdict submission while B succeeds.

Runner-stage deadline errors also need their own durable retry classes. Preserve caller cancellation separately, classify specialist child deadlines as `specialist_timeout` and judge child deadlines as `judge_timeout`, and do not let verification on an already-expired stage context relabel a runner timeout as a generic verification or judge failure.



## Curator normalization: worktree editing rule

The older worktree notes in this package describe both silent relative-path misrouting and loud absolute-path rejection. Treat the latest operational rule as authoritative: `apply_patch` is only for the primary workspace. For any worktree outside it, edit with a direct Python/heredoc operation after asserting the target path and unique replacement, then verify `git status` and `git diff` in both the worktree and primary checkout. Do not retry `apply_patch` against an external worktree path, and do not infer the active rule from older incident narratives.

## Shipping a secret file to a VPS via vault_exec (2026-08-24, CRM-AG)

Reliable pattern to place a locally generated secret file on a remote host through
`vault_exec` (vault injects the SSH key; you cannot scp a local file directly):

1. `base64 -w0 /tmp/secret.txt` locally.
2. `vault_exec credentialId=<ssh-cred> command=ssh args=["user@host", "echo <B64> | base64 -d | sudo tee /root/dir/secret.txt >/dev/null && sudo chmod 600 /root/dir/secret.txt && sudo wc -c /root/dir/secret.txt"]`.
3. Verify integrity with truncated hash on both sides: `md5sum file | cut -c1-8`
   (full md5 of a secret file gets redacted as high-entropy by the vault output
   scanner; an 8-char prefix passes through and is enough for a match check).

PITFALL — double decode: do NOT write the decoded bytes to a `.b64` staging file
and then `base64 -d` it again into the final file. That decodes twice and silently
corrupts the secret (observed: 21-byte password became 15 bytes of garbage, exit 0).
Decode exactly once, straight into the destination via `sudo tee`.

Also: passing one long `bash -c` style command as a single ssh arg works fine;
the earlier "exitCode -1 empty output" failures came from trying to pipe local
stdin into ssh through vault_exec (no stdin plumbing) — embed content in argv
instead.

# Consumer AI experience design

Use this skill when creating or revising a consumer-facing AI product, landing page, onboarding flow, or brand system. Optimize for felt relief, trust, comprehension, and memorable taste—not technical impressiveness.

## Core stance

A consumer is not buying an agent architecture. They are buying a better moment in their life. Lead with the human tension, show one recognizable outcome, and reveal the machinery only as proof. Treat empathy as product accuracy: name the burden without dramatizing it, explain what changes in plain language, and preserve the person's agency.

Use unease intentionally. Consumer AI often touches memory, ambient context, private conversations, and delegated action. A restrained dystopian edge can make that reality legible, but never aestheticize surveillance without also showing consent, control, boundaries, and reversibility.

## Required workflow

1. Read the product evidence and distinguish shipped capability, prototype, roadmap, and aspiration. Never turn aspiration into a present-tense claim.
2. Write the page's single human promise in one sentence. If it contains framework names, model names, protocols, or infrastructure language, rewrite it.
3. Choose three concrete daily moments that prove the promise. Prefer native phone messages, briefs, reminders, and recognizable artifacts over abstract AI particles or generic dashboards.
4. Establish deterministic tokens for type, spacing, radius, color, motion, and surface hierarchy before composing sections.
5. Build the story in this order: human promise → recognizable proof → daily outcomes → control/privacy → how it quietly works → honest availability → one low-friction CTA.
6. Verify keyboard use, focus visibility, semantics, mobile composition, reduced motion, contrast, overflow, console state, and production build.
7. Run the bounded Poetiq loop below. Record every material failure and its prevention rule.

## Poetiq critique loop

Run no more than three passes unless a real blocker remains:

- Observe: capture desktop and mobile renders and extract the visible copy/interactive tree.
- Verify: test the explicit acceptance checks and the lint rules in this skill.
- Diagnose: identify the smallest cause, not a vague aesthetic symptom.
- Refine: make the narrowest change that improves the user outcome without adding ornamental complexity.
- Preserve learning: append one row to the mistake ledger with symptom, root cause, detection signal, fix, and prevention rule.

Stop when all hard checks pass and later passes produce only subjective churn. Self-improvement means retaining validated rules; it does not mean endless redesign.

## Deterministic taste rules

- One dominant emotional promise per viewport; one primary CTA label across the page.
- The first screen must identify the category, benefit, and availability state without requiring scroll.
- Use no more than two font families plus one mono face for real technical artifacts.
- Use a restrained neutral foundation and at most two signal colors. Signal color must encode meaning or action.
- Use a spacing scale, not arbitrary gaps. Favor breathing room around ideas and tighter grouping within components.
- Motion must explain state, hierarchy, or causality. No scroll-jacking; no essential information available only through animation; honor reduced motion.
- Show the product in a familiar context before explaining its internal architecture.
- Do not fabricate metrics, testimonials, logos, pricing, integrations, screenshots, or availability.
- Put privacy substantiation next to privacy claims. State what is local, what leaves the device, what is retained, what can be deleted, and what remains unbuilt.
- Preserve agency in copy: prefer “you choose,” “you can review,” and “nothing happens without…” over “always watching,” “autopilot,” or anthropomorphic dependency claims.
- Dystopian tension is permitted only when the same section resolves it with visible user control.

## Consumer copy lint

Fail copy that includes unexplained developer language (`MCP`, API, protocol, typed tools, runtime, COGS, substrate, accessibility tree) above the technical appendix. Fail vague superlatives, unsupported “private” or “secure” claims, and abstract future language without a concrete scene. Flag repeated headline ideas, more than one CTA verb, and paragraphs longer than three short sentences.

Prefer verbs attached to life: remember, prepare, find, finish, check, ask, review, undo. Prefer specific moments: “the promise you made in a message” over “context aggregation.”

## Visual and interaction lint

Hard failures: horizontal overflow at 390px; body text below 16px for primary prose; controls below 44px touch size; missing visible focus; unlabeled interactive controls; contrast below WCAG AA; autoplay audio; motion without reduced-motion handling; content hidden only for mobile without an equivalent; CTA that claims submission without a working destination.

Review warnings: more than three card styles; more than two simultaneous ambient animations; all sections using the same centered layout; decorative phone mockups that do not demonstrate causality; tiny uppercase labels carrying essential meaning; privacy content buried in the footer.

## Self-healing protocol

When a defect is found, do not merely patch the instance. Classify it as content, claim integrity, hierarchy, token drift, responsiveness, accessibility, interaction, performance, or trust. Add or strengthen a reusable lint/check only if it would have caught the defect without creating noisy false positives. Keep project-specific exceptions in the repository-local skill, not in this global skill.

Maintain a mistake ledger with: date, surface, symptom, root cause, detection method, correction, prevention rule, and verification evidence. Revisit unresolved rows before future redesigns. Never erase mistakes; mark them resolved and link the rule that prevents recurrence.

## Handoff requirements

Report the promise, audience, availability state, files changed, verification evidence, known product gaps, and which retained rules influenced the result. # Software-surface, prompt, and protocol reverse engineering

Use to audit proprietary or unexpectedly open CLIs/binaries, reconstruct browser-visible HTTP/RPC surfaces, and trace prompt/context from construction through provider wire payloads and durable conversation state. Keep acquisition isolated, traffic secret-safe, and every conclusion evidence-graded.

## Scope, acquisition, and static analysis
Respect repository instructions and user state. Never run vendor installers against the real home merely to acquire artifacts or replay captured mutations without authorization. Record artifact URL, time, headers, hashes, redirects, platform, architecture, version, and type; inspect manifests before extraction. Inventory commands, flags, paths, env vars, integrations, OAuth, token stores, models, telemetry, updates, endpoints, and dependencies. Extract bounded slices from minified bundles.

## Browser and RPC surface mining
Filter static/analytics noise before prioritizing business requests, mutations, JSON/protobuf, redirects, and failures. Reconstruct method, path, auth class, content type, schemas, and response classes. Distinguish Next.js API/RSC/server actions; deployment-specific action IDs are not stable APIs. Recover protobuf descriptors when possible and treat parser/status evidence cautiously: recognized framing never proves authorization. Require session-specific evidence for billing mode rather than inferring from generic checkout HTML.

## Prompt/context construction to wire
Search templates, literals, config, middleware, hooks, dynamic context, tool results, provider catalogs, caches, and fallbacks. Prove each candidate live by tracing call sites to the final request, recording ordering, role, conditions, replacement, profile routing, and provider translation. Distinguish prompt-only restrictions from handler enforcement and verify flags have read sites. Label findings source-proven, documentation-only, runtime-dependent, or unavailable; do not claim exact bytes without a captured artifact/hash.

## Ephemeral guidance and durable conversation state
Injected skills/capabilities may decorate an execution request but must not be persisted inside durable user messages. Persist a clean clone while preserving the provider request; otherwise wrappers compound, bloat history, and poison summaries. Title/summary generation must consume semantic content rather than runtime scaffolding, with specific self-healing for legacy poisoned metadata. Put universal provenance at the conversation-creation chokepoint, preserve caller metadata, clear process-scoped keys on clones, and never invent lineage for nonpersisted subagents.

## Model catalogs and dynamic probes
Treat catalogs as provenance-bearing signals, not proof of callability. Compare authenticated APIs, public catalogs, docs/pricing, CLI allowlists, and history; normalize aliases and classify callable, advertised, router-only, stale, compatibility, or inferred staging. Probe control and inference planes separately. Use fresh HOME/XDG/config sandboxes and snapshot filesystem/process/network state. Start with help/status/invalid input but assume startup can write or phone home. Prefer key logging, instrumentation, or narrow untracked patches over unsafe interception.

## Evidence, credentials, and typed clients
Sanitize URLs and print header names rather than secret values. Protect HARs and caches as credentials; use 0600 derivatives and rotate exposure. Grade conclusions and cite hashes, sanitized entry indexes, offsets, and observation times. Build typed clients only after auth and framing are established, with explicit token loading, redacted representations, timeouts, structured errors, verified refresh behavior, and mocked transport tests.

## Lifecycle-trigger forensics
For compaction, retries, summaries, and checkpointing, locating the threshold predicate is insufficient. Trace each call site to the request/query loop and prove which durable events are already present. Record whether evaluation occurs on user submission, before a provider request, during tool continuation, on assistant completion, or after persistence. Distinguish a predicate becoming true after an event from the product evaluating it at that event. In minified bundles, anchor on telemetry markers and lifecycle strings, then extract bounded slices around the enclosing loop and caller.

## Prompt-cache and context-economics forensics
Treat provider prompt caching as part of prompt/context wire forensics. Trace exact serialized order (typically tools → system → messages), emitted TTL, breakpoint placement/count, and byte stability. A mutation invalidates from its earliest position onward, so rewriting a middle region can force the preserved tail to be resent. Audit per-turn volatility, in-place marker mutation, compression/summarization, tool-result pruning, model-switch normalization, and all retroactive history edits before prescribing longer TTLs.

Measure cache reads, cache creation, fresh input, and TTL-specific creation fields by provider/schema and entrypoint. Zero read with whole-prefix creation is the pathological signature. Verify current provider API facts rather than stale beta-header guidance. Distinguish defaults from opt-in features. A smaller context limit may cost more if it triggers destructive compression more frequently. Inspect persisted telemetry before adding instrumentation; ensure diagnostics parse the current usage schema and use the TTL actually sent.

The former `llm-prompt-cache-economics` package is absorbed here. Do not recreate a narrow sibling. Load:
- `references/prompt-cache-audit-checklist.md` first for the ordered audit, pricing/API facts to re-verify, controlled reproduction, honest `unknown` classification, differential validation, and reporting rules.
- `references/prompt-cache-llxprt-case-study.md` and `references/prompt-cache-llxprt-case-study-detail.md` for the llxprt/Code Puppy evidence.

- `references/llxprt-case-study.md` and `references/swarm-case-study.md` as byte-for-byte provenance originals; prefer the `prompt-cache-*` versions for routine reading.

## Tool-history error accounting
When auditing tool or MCP failures from durable history, do not filter only transport-level failures. Wrappers can catch exceptions and return successful text payloads such as `Error: ...`, unsupported/stub messages, stale prior-call results, or contradictory state. Search failed metadata and successful payload bodies, then correlate requested tool/arguments with response shape to detect displacement. Report transport failures, application errors, unsupported capabilities, harness blocks, and agent misuse separately.

# Evidence-preserving data and model engineering

Use this class-level umbrella for evidence-preserving research, browser/API/filesystem acquisition, sensitive ingestion, deterministic transformation, dataset governance, model/agent evaluation, citation-grade synthesis, and audited report/document production. Preserve raw evidence and make every derivative traceable, reproducible, and policy-governed.

## Contracts, boundaries, and immutable evidence

Define sources, authorization, expected volume, retention, sensitive fields, consumers, failure semantics, and the exact claims outputs support. Separate acquisition, transformation, storage, analysis, evaluation, training, and publication trust boundaries. Treat HARs, cookies, browser databases, model traces, and crash dumps as credential-bearing until sanitized; use isolated profiles and least-privilege credentials.

Write an immutable raw artifact before normalization whenever policy permits. Record locator, acquisition time, request/capture identity, tool/schema versions, content type, size, hash, and redaction or truncation. Keep source and ingestion timestamps separate. Use stable identities and content hashes for idempotent retries. Never overwrite raw evidence with cleaned output; link every normalized row, feature, label, report, or benchmark result to its raw artifact and transformation version.

## Acquisition and transformation pipelines

Prefer replayable captures—sanitized HAR/network logs, DOM snapshots, exports, or bounded API responses—over screenshots except when visual state is itself evidence. Capture redirects, pagination, response classes, and relevant nonsecret headers. Never replay mutations or authenticated requests without authorization.

Route secrets through designated vault/encryption interfaces. Validate MIME/type and size, quarantine malformed or active content, use bounded concurrency and resumable checkpoints, and record partial failures. Make transformations deterministic where feasible; version code, schemas, parsing rules, dependencies, and reference data. Preserve original values when normalization is lossy, treat parse failures and quality flags as data, and define correction, deletion, tombstone, and late-arrival semantics.

For ordered high-volume streams, checkpoint on a stable monotonic event ID rather than timestamp alone. Commit each bounded page before advancing the cursor and test restart, duplicate replay, equal timestamps, empty/short pages, and stalled cursors. In shell pipelines, propagate producer failure and reject zero-byte captures before content addressing. Inaccessible manifest partitions may be continued only under explicit partial-run policy: preserve ordinals, emit durable dispositions, exit nonzero, and withhold global completion.

Use ordered schema migrations and test empty, prior-version, and interrupted states. Reconcile source counts, hashes, accepted/rejected records, uniqueness, integrity, distributions, and sampled trace-back. Publish completeness bounds and known gaps. Before finalizing in a shared worktree, coordinate with other writers, require the producer's completion marker, stage an explicit manifest, and verify remote refs; never convert a live checkpoint into a false final state.

## Dataset governance

Maintain a dataset card with purpose, collection window, source policy, license/consent, inclusion rules, sensitive attributes, transformations, limitations, splits, and retention obligations. Keep train, validation, test, red-team, and production-feedback sets distinct. Split on the true leakage unit, detect exact and near duplicates, tag synthetic content with generator/configuration/parents, and never silently recycle evaluation cases into training.

## Reproducible agent and model evaluation

Define hypothesis, task population, metrics, graders, stopping policy, and baseline before experiments. Record model/provider identity, prompts, tools/skills, retrieval snapshot, code and environment revisions, dependencies, seeds, sampling settings, budgets, credentials class/path provenance, and timestamps. Preserve per-trial transcripts, tool calls, timing, costs, grader inputs/outputs, and structured failure classes. Use paired tasks and repeated trials; report uncertainty, exclusions, and sensitivity.

Validate the verifier before model spend: make an Oracle pass, run install-only and direct-model smokes, preserve candidate artifacts after timeout, and distinguish infrastructure, strategy, execution, and verifier failures. A uniform result across arms usually indicts the instrument. Normalize semantically irrelevant whitespace, score invariants rather than hardcoded names, enforce only observable constraints, print every failure reason, and pair every relaxation with a negative test. Re-run oracles, unit tests, and archived real runs after scorer edits. Include opposite-polarity and mixed cases so constant always-merge/always-keep policies cannot pass for the wrong reason. Derive synthetic cases from an independently audited corpus rather than inventing traps and answer keys together.

For Harbor and similar containerized benchmarks, load `references/harbor-novel-problem-benchmark.md` first, then only the task-family or operational references needed. Preflight task networking, installed-agent environment delivery, credential path, and credential rotation window. A launcher timeout may leave Docker execution alive; reconcile result files, containers, and exact PIDs before rerunning, preserve partial work, and stage the immutable verifier if recovery is authorized. Never use broad `pgrep -f` waits that can match their own shell; poll an exact PID or completion artifact.

Protect hidden tests, inspect contamination, blind human review where practical, and calibrate automated judges against human labels and adversarial cases. Promote datasets, models, or pipelines only after reproducibility, quality, privacy/security, rollback, and cost/latency gates pass.

## Calibrated critique and manual orchestration

For subjective deliverables, run deterministic checks first, then use an isolated judge with one candidate, a demanding domain persona, a priority rubric, and validated machine-readable output. Turn defects into a binding revision brief with acceptance tests; preserve versions and re-observe the live/rendered artifact. Treat narration, sentiment, or rubric scores as markers until outcome-calibrated, not as proof of competence.

Before automating a multi-stage agent pipeline, manually orchestrate 2–4 real inputs and prove at least two stages independently. Automation compresses a known-good process; it does not discover one. When dogfooding an interactive product, use its real TTY/daemon/peer path and verify peer registration, live state, completion artifacts, viewport/session state, and production rendering. Bound open-ended instructions.

For behavioral studies, mine the raw durable conversation store when indexed search omits thinking, tool-error taxonomy, hook context, model identity, or message/tool-call co-location. Deduplicate compaction lineages by proven logical identity; aggregate usage by lineage root and response deduplication key. Condition on the blocked alternative and separate hook blocks from genuine failures. Stratify by date, model family, visible prose, and private reasoning. Instrument echo on content words and test all language markers against actual recovery outcomes.

## Evidence-grounded research and citation synthesis

Freeze entity, date, timezone, source scope, and output contract. Run diverse targeted queries; distinguish official statements, analysis, rumor, and sentiment; attach source plus publication/retrieval date to every material or volatile claim. Preserve NDJSON and raw captures. Prefer primary sources and replayable captures, cross-check consequential claims independently, expose conflicts and single-source assertions, and never invent missing prices, features, quotes, or statistics.

For exhaustive screens, prove set equality between the frozen manifest and analyzed rows plus documented exclusions. For live marketplaces, validate query semantics and enumerate the timestamped visible universe before treating an empty result as absence. For market data, resolve retrieval time into exchange timezone, report the latest returned bar and whether it is completed, and never call it the requested date's close unless the session has closed and the response proves it.

## Report and document production

Define claims, citations, figures, literal commands, caveats, provenance requirements, and page constraints before rendering LaTeX/R/TikZ, Markdown, HTML/SVG, or PDF. Build reproducibly and inspect every page for clipping, overflow, blank bands, contrast, orphans, distortion, omissions, and copy/paste mutations. Preflight every non-core package and binary (`kpsewhich` or equivalent), compile enough times to resolve references, inspect logs, and render pages as images: clipping, float-only pages, widows, and template whitespace defects may produce no build warning.

Use isolated workspaces, durable logs, bounded review, explicit stage contracts, and truthful partial-result retention. Write structured outputs atomically; make HTML self-contained and escaped; verify temporary PDFs before same-directory rename. Preserve automated finding severity as provenance but assess exploitability, impact, likelihood, and confidence separately. Load `references/latex-r-report-toolchain.md`, `references/report-studio-pipeline.md`, or `references/sac-report-renderer.md` only when those workflows apply.

## Website search and analytics audits

Treat SEO, SERP visibility, Core Web Vitals, schema, consent, GA4/GTM/Meta events, and custom visitor logging as evidence-producing measurement work. Establish domains, markets, language, audit date, and authorization; use read-only bounded crawls and redact cookies, visitor IDs, IPs, analytics identifiers, and query-string PII. Separate confirmed observations, likely conclusions, and hypotheses. Verify redirects, robots and sitemaps, canonicals, structured data, rendered content, performance, and actual network event payloads—never infer a working pixel from a script tag. Test duplicate events, consent behavior, attribution, and measurement integrity, then report reproducible evidence and prioritized remediation without submitting lead-generating forms.

## Browser evidence recovery

When Chrome MCP `computer(action="screenshot")` returns only an opaque screenshot ID and no export path, the durable conversation transcript may contain the JPEG bytes as a base64 image content block. Search the current workspace's raw transcript store (`~/.swarmos/conversations/<base64-workspace>/*.json`) for the screenshot ID. In the matching tool result, select the image content block, decode it into an evidence file, and validate with both `file` and an image decoder such as ImageMagick `identify`. Preserve the full capture as raw evidence and make presentation crops as derivatives. Never dump base64 to user-visible output. This is a recovery path, not a substitute for a first-class screenshot export API.

When a Google Drive folder's accessibility tree shows an empty item grid after loading, do not conclude the folder is empty. Read the rendered grid or `document.body.innerText` in page context and record the folder title plus visible filenames before opening artifacts. This catches wrong-folder links early and avoids mistaking UI-loading or accessibility gaps for missing evidence.

## Verification and deliverables

Test parser fixtures, idempotent replay, duplicate delivery, pagination, malformed inputs, redaction, vault failure, interrupted transactions, migration, deletion propagation, and sampled trace-back. Exercise a small end-to-end fixture before scale and restart testing.

Deliver architecture/trust boundaries, source and authorization inventory, lineage and schemas, security/retention policy, migration/retry design, quality checks, dataset/evaluation card, reproducible run manifest, failure ledger, rendered-output audit, and explicit evidence-backed limitations.

New session-specific incidents, provider quirks, benchmark cases, and host inventories belong in `references/<topic>.md` with at most a one-line pointer here; do not append another long section to this body.


## Criterion-specific evidence integrity for exhaustive UI audits

Set equality proves only coverage, not truth. A criterion may be marked PASS only when its linked evidence specifically demonstrates that criterion; a generic screen capture plus a green module test is not sufficient for claims about named seed records, exact values, cross-module presence, role behavior, or downstream persistence. Before accepting an exhaustive browser audit, cross-check summary claims against independent postflight counts and mutually dependent criteria. Treat contradictions as verifier failures—for example, zero live records cannot support PASS for importing named records, and an absent destination screen cannot support PASS for a record also existing there. Downgrade unsupported rows to PARTIAL/BLOCKED/FAIL or collect targeted evidence, then regenerate totals, failure ledgers, hashes, and summary. # Grill Me

Adapted from Paul Razvan Berg's MIT-licensed `grill-me` skill at `paulrberg/agent-skills`, pinned and reviewed at commit `07ea66325524edd18ddcd70e2e552a6c47738887`. Preserve this attribution through future maintenance.

Use this domain-independent method to stress-test requirements, plans, designs, architecture, rollout, or implementation scope until every material branch is resolved. The phrase “grill me” is an alias, not the only trigger.

## Decision workflow

1. Extract the objective, constraints, assumptions, evidence, and decisions already made. Investigate facts discoverable from the codebase or supplied material instead of asking the user.
2. Maintain a running record with decision, chosen option, rationale, dependencies, and consequences. Do not reopen a settled decision unless new evidence conflicts with it.
3. Ask exactly one question at a time. Format it as `### 🔥 Decision <N> — <topic>`, followed by `Recommended`, `Why`, `Tradeoff`, and `Question`.
4. Choose the highest-leverage unresolved branch—the answer that constrains the most downstream choices.
5. After each answer, acknowledge `✅ Recorded: <choice> — <consequence>`. Show settled/open counts when useful, but never a percentage because the tree may grow.
6. Cover scope, users, interfaces, data/state, failure modes, security, operations, migration, testing, rollout, ownership, and stopping criteria only where material.
7. Finish only when every material branch has a recorded decision or an explicitly accepted unknown with an owner and resolution point.

## Final decision record

Return `### ✅ Decision record` with a decision/choice/rationale/consequence table, then `### ⚠️ Risks`, accepted unknowns with owner and resolution point, material rejected alternatives, and `### 🏁 Completion criteria`. Do not end with another question.

## Orchestrator adaptation

When implementation is already authorized and the user supplied a prioritized backlog, do not re-ask settled questions. Apply the same discipline internally to select a granular worker task with explicit scope, non-goals, files or subsystem, acceptance criteria, verification, rollback, and stop conditions. Ask the user only when a genuinely unresolved choice would materially alter implementation.

When choosing from a multi-domain audit, preserve the user’s named outcome as the primary category. A high-severity adjacent issue is not a substitute for the requested result. Before dispatch, state in one sentence how the selected task directly advances that result.

## Interaction modes

Default to one-question-at-a-time conversation. If the user explicitly rejects the available prompt UI for ongoing visual or logical comparisons, use a persistent chooser service instead of repeatedly retrying an unfit interaction tool. If the user wants unattended resumption after deciding, add a durable catch-up-and-wait mechanism rather than relying on memory or a pure lossy push event.

Load `references/live-chooser-and-dormant-trigger.md` only for chooser APIs, durable progress state, polling/WebSocket wakeups, race handling, background-process survival, and cheap verification of delegated nested-model features. Keep those implementation details out of this class-level protocol.

## Scope and handoff

This skill owns decision elicitation, recording, and closure—not execution. Hand off after decisions are settled:

- General implementation, testing, GitHub, and release work → `software-engineering-and-delivery`
- Swarm SDK/TUI/Desktop/providers/tools/tasks/autogenskills → `swarm-stack-engineering`
- Clover infrastructure and production operations → `clover-platform-operations`

- Bounded reads or repository search → `read-source-files` / `search-codebase`

Conversely, if work in one of those domains stalls on an unresolved material tradeoff, return here rather than guessing.

## Curator boundary

This is already a class-level reusable method. Do not fold it into a single domain umbrella merely because one implementation used it there. ## Reading absolute MFU out of a co-authored partner blog post, not just relative uplift

A vendor blog headline number like "lifted MFU by up to ~65%" is a **relative** improvement, not an
absolute MFU. Before citing it as "Nebius/X discloses Y% MFU," scroll past the headline to the
results table — partner-co-authored posts (e.g. a joint Nebius+PyTorch DeepSeek-V3/TorchTitan
recipe) frequently contain an actual **before/after absolute MFU table** buried mid-post:

| Model | MFU without optimization | MFU with optimization | Relative gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-16B (64 experts) | 8.29% | 13.64% | ~65% |
| DeepSeek V3-671B (256 experts) | 11.22% | 13.99% | ~25% |

This is a **real, citable, absolute MFU figure** (training workload, specific GPU count/generation
stated) — treat it as "verified: found" for an MFU/utilization research question, not "not found,"
even though it wasn't volunteered as a headline metric and is training- not inference-side MFU.
Always fetch the full page (curl -A "Mozilla/5.0" + strip tags, or a browser tool) rather than
trusting a search-engine summary — summaries reliably surface the flashy relative-% headline and
drop the absolute-number table underneath it.

## Classifying hyperscaler offtake contracts as take-or-pay without verbatim "fixed-price"/"cost-plus"

SEC 6-K filings and trade press almost never use the literal words "fixed-price" or "cost-plus" for
a neocloud↔hyperscaler GPU capacity deal. Instead, classify from structural tells that are usually
present:
- **"Take-or-pay" / minimum-commitment language** — the counterparty (Microsoft, Meta, etc.) is
  contractually obligated to pay for committed capacity whether or not it's fully used → this is a
  **fixed-revenue-to-the-provider** structure, not usage-metered, regardless of what it's called.
- **Provider-side financing tells**: if trade press states the *provider* (e.g. Nebius) is raising
  debt "secured against the contract" / "against contracted cash flows," that only makes sense if
  the contract delivers a predictable, non-variable revenue stream to collateralize — strong
  secondary evidence for fixed/take-or-pay, not cost-plus passthrough.
- **Termination-for-delivery-failure clauses** (counterparty can terminate a specific "GPU Service"
  tranche if the provider misses delivery dates) describe a **committed-capacity** deal, not a
  metered-usage one.
- State the finding as "**structurally take-or-pay / fixed-capacity commitment**, though the filing
  does not use the term 'fixed-price' verbatim" — this is a legitimate, cite-able classification,
  not a guess, when 2+ of the tells above are present. Do not report "not found" just because the
  exact contract-law term isn't quoted; report the structural classification with its basis.

# macOS host and iOS lab operations

Use this class-level workflow for macOS hosts that run Xcode, WebDriverAgent, idb, pymobiledevice3, Maestro, simulators, or physical-device automation. Separate host reachability, console-session state, developer-tool readiness, and device readiness; success in one layer does not prove the next.

## Authorization and safety

Before disabling FileVault, changing login policy, resetting an account password, performing a major OS upgrade, rebooting a shared host, modifying signing identities, or exposing remote-control services, obtain explicit authorization and define rollback. Never persist Apple ID, administrator, signing, or device credentials in plaintext. Route secrets through the approved vault and avoid echoing them in commands, logs, or process arguments.

Inventory active users and automation jobs before disruptive work. Preserve current OS/Xcode versions, disk-encryption state, network identity, login policy, available disk space, and recovery route. A remote-only host needs a tested path back after reboot; do not assume SSH or a GUI-session VPN will return automatically.

## Reachability and session model

Prefer SSH for shell work and Screen Sharing/Remote Management only for GUI-required steps. Verify Remote Login and the intended SSH allowlist. Distinguish four states:

1. the Mac is powered and network-reachable;
2. SSH is listening and the account is authorized;
3. a user owns the console GUI session;
4. per-user applications such as Tailscale or App Store are initialized.

Auto-login is not Apple ID sign-in. App Store authentication, 2FA, license dialogs, privacy prompts, and some developer-account operations remain interactive. GUI-session network clients may disappear or re-register when the console user changes, so resolve the current node rather than trusting a cached address.

## FileVault and auto-login

Check `fdesetup status` and `sudo sysadminctl -autologin status`. FileVault normally prevents unattended auto-login. Disabling it is a security-policy change, not a troubleshooting convenience; explain the tradeoff and obtain consent. If authorized, wait for decryption to complete before relying on auto-login.

Use `sudo sysadminctl -autologin set -userName <user> -password <password>` where supported and verify the resulting policy. Prefer supported interfaces. Treat direct `/etc/kcpassword` manipulation as an exceptional, security-sensitive fallback requiring explicit authorization and a tested rollback. Prove behavior after reboot with the actual console user and restored network access.

## macOS upgrades

Record `sw_vers`, architecture, disk space, power state, FileVault state, and the target Xcode compatibility requirement. Enumerate updates with `softwareupdate --list` and major installers with `softwareupdate --list-full-installers`; verify current Apple compatibility data rather than relying on historical examples.

For a point update, `sudo softwareupdate -ia --restart --agree-to-license` may be appropriate. For a major upgrade, fetch the exact full installer and use its `startosinstall` interface, checking current flags for Intel versus Apple Silicon. Run long work under a durable supervisor, keep the host on power, capture logs, and expect one or more reboots. Never call an upgrade complete until the host returns through the intended remote path and postflight checks pass.

## Xcode and command-line tools

Prefer a reproducible, authenticated download path such as `xcodes` or an Apple Developer download over brittle App Store UI automation. If the App Store is required, account sign-in and 2FA are per-user GUI state and may need a human. After installation:

```sh
sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode.app
sudo xcodebuild -license accept
sudo xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch
xcodebuild -version
```

Command Line Tools alone do not provide full simulator/device support. Xcode itself may install without simulator runtimes; inspect `xcrun simctl list runtimes` and download the required platform explicitly if absent. Preserve multiple Xcode installations with versioned app names when rollback matters.

## Signing, simulators, and physical devices

Treat these as separate readiness gates:

- **Signing:** inspect available identities and team/provisioning configuration without exporting private keys. Build a minimal authorized target.
- **Simulator:** verify runtimes, create or select a device by UDID, boot it, and run a minimal test. Parse structured `simctl --json` output without splitting device names on spaces.
- **Physical device:** verify trust/pairing, Developer Mode, tunnel/service prerequisites, device visibility, signing, and a minimal WDA or equivalent launch.
- **Automation protocol:** prove the actual RPC/driver path with a cheap command before a full suite.

Do not infer physical-device behavior from Simulator. Settings panes, battery data, permissions, push notifications, hardware sensors, and trust workflows differ. XCUIAutomation APIs may require main-thread execution; if an RPC host accepts a connection and then hangs or asserts, verify thread affinity before blaming selectors or transport.

## Verification and recovery

After any change, capture:

```sh

uname -m
fdesetup status
sudo sysadminctl -autologin status
xcode-select -p
xcodebuild -version
xcrun simctl list runtimes
xcrun simctl list devices | head
xcrun xctrace list devices
```

Also verify the actual console user, SSH after reboot, current VPN/tailnet identity, free disk space, required signing identity, one simulator smoke, and—when relevant—one physical-device smoke. ## 13. Issues/measurability tracking system (added 2026-07-25)

For a vault that generates research, "we don't know X yet" tends to live only in a prose
"Explicit gaps" paragraph that nobody revisits — the same gap gets silently re-discovered every
time a thesis is re-checked. Fix: a first-class `type: issue` note per gap, with a **measurability
contract** in frontmatter: `measurable: true|false`, `measure-method:` (the specific source/
mechanism that would resolve it — a filing type, a named benchmark/leaderboard, a search method),
`recheck:` (cadence: weekly/monthly/quarterly/on-earnings/on-filing/on-event:<desc>), and
`last-checked:` (distinct from `updated:`, which changes on any edit). Add both a structured field
AND a scan tag (`is-measurable`/`not-measurable`) — neither substitutes for the other, one is for
Bases/Dataview queries, one is for eyeballing in Obsidian.

**Lifecycle reuses the vault's existing archive mechanism exactly, no new status vocabulary
needed**: open issue = `status: active` in a new top-level `issues/` folder (parallel to
`research/`/`resources/`/`projects/`/`areas/`); resolved = move the file unchanged to
`archive/issues/`, `status: archived`, add a `## Resolution` section. This is the same "archive =
move + set status: archived" rule the vault likely already has for everything else — don't invent
parallel machinery.

**Filing an issue is mandatory whenever a gap is found** (a swarm -p worker's own "Explicit gaps,"
a weekly thesis-health review, a company gap-analysis) — before that research pass is considered
done. This is the actual mechanism that stops gaps from being silently re-discovered.

### Why NOT a global tool hook ("catalyst hooks" that don't cascade)
A tempting design is a `~/.swarmos/hooks.json` custom_hook that fires on relevant tool calls to
surface open/overdue issues. **Reject this for any multi-agent vault** — hooks.json is global and
fires on every matching tool call in every session, including an unrelated parallel headless
research worker, and a `block_on_output` action forces exactly the cascading diversion you're
trying to avoid in one worker by way of a hook meant for a different one. The safe, proven
alternative: extend the vault's own read-only triage script (see e.g. `meta/scripts/triage.sh`)
with new checks (issue missing `measurable:`, `measurable: true` issues whose `recheck` cadence
is overdue vs `last-checked`, decision notes missing a required section) and invoke it only at
deliberate checkpoints (session start, daily/weekly cron reviews, pre-launch of any research
worker) — it can never interrupt a parallel agent because nothing calls it automatically
mid-tool-call. This gets you the enforcement without any blocking-hook cascade risk.

## 14. Range/timeline/bound-and-impact contract for decision theses (added 2026-07-25)

A thesis that only states a directional belief ("X will happen") without explicit bounds invites
unfalsifiable vibes-based confirmation over time. Require one fixed-column markdown table per
`type: decision` note — `| Sector | Country/region | Macro impact | Micro (company) impact | Low
bound | Base case | High bound | Timeline |` — one row per distinct claim. Order-of-magnitude
disagreement between sources on a bound is itself a finding: preserve it as a wide bound, never
average it away. Apply going forward to new/updated theses; append a first version as a dated
addendum to pre-existing theses rather than rewriting their bodies (same append-only principle as
every other evidence update). A read-only triage check (grep for the required section heading)
self-surfaces which existing theses still lack the table — cheap, no separate tracking needed.

## 15. Company capability-gap-analysis pattern (added 2026-07-25)

A reusable `type: snapshot` template for comparing a company's **actual** realized output/
utilization against its **theoretical potential** given already-disclosed supply (fleet size,
capex, power), its **contract-imposed ceiling** (fixed-price/take-or-pay vs cost-plus — this single
fact determines whether an efficiency investment would even move the company's own margin), and
its **optimized potential** if it invested in a capability (e.g. kernel/algorithm optimization)
peer companies already have. Template sections: Actual / Potential / Contract ceiling / Optimized
potential / Gap stated plainly / Open questions filed as issues. **Do not guess the unknown
cells** — file each concrete unresolved sub-question as a `type: issue` (§13) instead of estimating
it, then research it as a follow-up pass. Worked example and validated end-to-end in this vault
(Nebius, 2026-07-25): the analysis correctly identified 3 measurable sub-questions (does the
company have the capability at all, what's its realized utilization, is its revenue contract-
floored or margin-ceilinged) and a live follow-up research pass answered all 3 with primary
sources (GitHub org + engineering blog + SEC 6-K filing text), **overturning the analysis's own
initial hypothesis** (the company turned out to have real, if narrower, Side-A capability) rather
than confirming a guess — exactly the value of filing genuine open questions instead of asserting.

## 16. Default execution model: swarm -p research workers as standard practice (added 2026-07-25)

Once a vault has grown a research-heavy AGENTS.md, codify headless `swarm -p` workers as the
DEFAULT way to execute any multi-topic/multi-source research pass (roughly 3+ independent
sub-questions), not a special-case tool. Document it as its own AGENTS.md section with two gates:

**Pre-launch**: define scope explicitly (which open issues this run addresses — check first,
never silently re-derive a tracked gap), use the verified no-recursion recipe
(`--disable-tools Subagent,Delegate,SubagentOutput,DelegateOutput,BackgroundTask,TaskOutput,
multi_agent_wait,wait_for_agent`), do NOT pass `--clean-agent` (the worker needs the vault's own
AGENTS.md/skills to auto-load so it files things the same way an interactive session would),
require incremental `Filed-by: agent` commits so partial progress survives a turn-budget cutoff.

**Post-run**: every "explicit gap" the worker reports becomes a `type: issue` note before the pass
counts as done; every issue the worker actually answered gets resolved/archived; and — the step
most worth stating explicitly — **the orchestrating session does a corrective synthesis pass
before trusting the worker's own framing**. A worker's prompt can subtly conflate what it was
asked to measure with what actually matters (observed directly in this vault: a demand-economics
research prompt led with price data, but the real thesis was a volume/intelligence-throughput
claim with price as a downstream variable — caught only by the orchestrating session reading the
output critically afterward, not by the worker itself, and not by the prompt design either).
Treat a headless worker's final report as a lead to verify, not a deliverable to rubber-stamp.

# read-source-files

Use the platform's native file-reading and listing facilities for safe, bounded, side-effect-free inspection. Prefer absolute paths, validate positive ordered line ranges, and retain line numbers when evidence matters. For large or unfamiliar files, inspect size or structure first and read bounded non-overlapping chunks. Do not dump generated, minified, lock, log, database, or binary content unless required.

## Credential-aware reading

Treat `.env`, vault, credential, private-key, token, secret, and production-config paths as sensitive even when the user authorizes their use. Do not print their raw contents into tool output merely to discover available configuration. First inspect filenames and then list variable/key names with values redacted (for example, transform `NAME=value` to `NAME=REDACTED`), or source the file inside a scoped command that consumes the secret without echoing it. Read a raw secret value only when the task strictly requires the value in model context; prefer secure execution and ensure secrets never appear in user-facing output, command output, logs, URLs, or process arguments when avoidable.

## Single-file mode

Read the requested file or range with native tools. If a range extends beyond EOF, return the available lines. Distinguish not-found, permission, directory-vs-file, binary/unsupported, and truncation errors. If output truncates, continue with bounded, non-overlapping chunks and do not imply omitted content was inspected.

## Multi-file or directory mode

Resolve the intended directory, list entries, filter to relevant files, exclude directories/generated/vendor/binary trees unless in scope, and read targets individually in deterministic order when practical. Do not silently traverse symlinked directories or repeatedly read one underlying file through aliases.

## Safety and evidence

Reading must remain side-effect free. Never use a mutating command merely to inspect content. Cite the exact path and line range actually inspected when supporting a review or diagnosis, and distinguish evidence from inference. If one file fails, report it and continue with the rest unless no requested file can be processed.

## Reading past a tool's output ceiling

Bounded-read discipline is the only way to inspect a document larger than a
tool's output limit. When a viewer or lister refuses a payload with a
"result too large" error, do not conclude the content is unavailable.

Two routes, in order of preference:

1. **Paged reads through the same tool.** Many viewers accept `offset`/`limit`
   (or equivalent) and report the total size in their header. This is cheaper
   and safer than reaching for the filesystem. A tiny `limit` is also the
   cheapest way to MEASURE something without retrieving it.
2. **Direct bounded reads of the underlying file**, in non-overlapping ranges,
   when the tool has no paging.

Either way, report the exact ranges inspected and never imply the unread
remainder was reviewed.

Re-check the paging route before falling back: a tool that once refused a large
payload outright may have gained `offset`/`limit` since the last attempt.

# search-codebase

This is the unified, canonical foundational skill for searching repositories and source trees.

## Curator retention policy

Do **not** archive or consolidate this skill based only on age or stale/unused-day heuristics. It is the canonical subsumer of legacy grep/search variants, remains actively used, and is stable platform infrastructure that may be invoked implicitly. Archive it only if the platform removes or replaces its repository-search mechanism.

Being flagged by an age/overlap heuristic despite recent active use is expected and is not a defect. The recurring proposal to merge this skill with `read-source-files` into one "codebase navigation" umbrella has been evaluated and rejected on six consecutive passes; the rationale is recorded once in `swarm-stack-engineering/references/autogenskills-library-map.md`. Do not re-derive it.

Maintenance instruction for future curator passes: **rewrite this section in place.** Do not append another dated revalidation note — a stack of them turns a stable primitive into a changelog. Last revalidated 2026-08-11.

It subsumes these archived legacy skills: repo-grep, code-search-repo, grep-search, grep_search, search-code, code-search, read-and-search-file, code-search-pattern, fastapi-streaming-response-fix-search, search-markdown, search-env-var-resolution, and fastapi-grep-read.

Use the platform's native grep/search facility when available. Adapt parameter names to the actual tool schema rather than assuming the illustrative names below are literal. Fall back to a suitable repository search command only when native search cannot express the request.

## Conceptual inputs
- `pattern` (required): regex to search for.
- `path` (optional): file or directory scope; default to the confirmed repository root.
- `file_pattern` (optional): glob such as `*.go` or `*.ts`.
- `max_matches` (optional): result cap; default around 200 to avoid excessive output.
- `context_lines` (optional): surrounding lines per match; default 0.
- `output_mode` (optional): `files` for unique paths or `content` for path, line, and text; default `content`.
- `literal` (optional): when supported, treat the pattern as fixed text rather than regex. Never silently change modes.

## Procedure
1. Establish the intended repository root and scope. In monorepos, worktrees, or duplicate source trees, confirm that the search targets the live tree rather than an unrelated parent or stale copy.
2. Call the available search tool with the pattern, scope, result mode, cap, and supported file filter.
3. Prefer `files` mode when only locations are needed. Use `content` for definitions, references, or evidence.
4. If context is requested but the search tool cannot return it directly, read bounded ranges around matching lines with the canonical `read-source-files` skill.
5. Return concise, deduplicated results. Preserve deterministic path/line order when practical.
6. If there are no results, state the exact scope, filters, ignore behavior, and pattern mode searched. Consider likely variants—case, naming convention, extension, generated location—only when relevant; do not claim a symbol is absent from the whole repository after a narrow search.
7. If a broad query hits the result cap or tool output is truncated, say so and narrow by path, file type, or a more specific expression rather than implying completeness.

## Search strategy
- Start with exact identifiers, error strings, filenames, config keys, or route fragments before broad conceptual terms.
- For an unfamiliar feature, search definitions plus call sites/imports/registrations. A filename or declaration match alone does not prove runtime use.
- Use alternation or several targeted searches for naming variants rather than one overly broad wildcard expression.
- For renamed or removed behavior, search current source first, then version-control history only if the task calls for historical evidence.
- Search hidden or ignored files only when configuration, CI, credentials metadata, generated artifacts, or repository internals are explicitly relevant.
- Exclude vendor, dependency, build, cache, minified, binary, and generated trees by default unless they are in scope.
- When a native tool and a command-line fallback differ in ignore-file, symlink, hidden-file, multiline-regex, or encoding behavior, state the effective behavior rather than treating the results as interchangeable.

## Safety and correctness
- Treat the pattern and path as data. In command-line fallbacks, quote arguments safely and use `--` before user-controlled patterns or paths where the command supports it; avoid shell interpolation.
- Preserve regex semantics; do not silently convert regex to literal search or vice versa.
- Report invalid-regex errors distinctly from a valid search with zero matches.
- Do not expose secret values merely because a search finds them. Report the path and category safely, redacting sensitive content when appropriate.
- A capped, filtered, ignored-file-skipping, permission-limited, binary-skipping, symlink-limited, or truncated search is not exhaustive; label those limitations.
- Respect repository boundaries and do not broaden into home directories or sibling workspaces without a task-specific reason.

## Evidence and completeness invariant

Separate discovery from proof: search results identify candidates, while bounded source reads establish behavior. Never infer runtime reachability, absence, or completeness solely from one declaration match or one capped query. Record the exact root, path filters, pattern mode, and cap when findings support an audit or review.

Corollary for any search-like tool, not just this one: **an empty result from a
higher-level search API is inconclusive, not proof of absence.** Before
reporting "not found", confirm the tool actually indexes the corpus you mean,
and fall back to a lower-level search over the raw store. The
`HistorySearch` case below is the worked example of this failure mode.

## Examples
- Function definition: regex `func NewClient`, file pattern `*.go`.
- Exact error text: literal `context deadline exceeded`.
- TypeScript interfaces: regex `export interface`, file pattern `*.ts`, cap 50.
- TODO with context: regex `TODO\\(user\\)`, context 3.
- Location only: use `files` mode for a unique list of matching paths.
- Definition plus references: search the exact symbol, then inspect its defining file and bounded call-site ranges.

## Recovering facts from prior conversations when HistorySearch returns nothing

`HistorySearch` can return zero results for queries whose answer is demonstrably
present in the stored transcripts — including `scope: "all"` with plain
high-signal keywords. Treat an empty `HistorySearch` result as **inconclusive,
not as proof of absence**, and fall back to searching the raw conversation
store directly.

# Software engineering and delivery

Use for repository-level engineering changes that span implementation, build and test workflows, release integration, or cross-cutting product behavior. Keep changes scoped, evidence-based, reversible, and verified at the narrowest useful layer before broad suites.

## Repository and change method

Map the repository and its build/test contracts before editing. Preserve user changes and worktree boundaries. State the intended blast radius, identify generated files and external dependencies, and use focused tests first. Do not claim a full pass when tooling, platform, or environment limits coverage; report exact commands and outcomes.

When parallel lanes use isolated worktrees, treat each worktree—not the shared main checkout—as the authoritative state for that lane. Before a coordinator, reviewer, or provider planner calls a finding current, reconcile the target lane's status and diff; otherwise label evidence as main-branch, production, or historical. Never overwrite a lane conclusion with a shared-checkout assumption.

## Delivery and GitHub lifecycle

Use isolated worktrees for parallel or protected-branch work. Keep commits surgical and reviewable, preserve Git LFS behavior, and create pull requests only after focused verification. Treat branch protection, required checks, conversation resolution, merge-base selection, and workflow permissions as separate gates. Never smuggle untrusted branch-controlled values into shell code; validate identifiers and pass them through environment variables. Separate build, artifact integrity, publish, and deploy permissions, and require explicit deployment authorization for production mutation.

## Language and product sections

### Go engineering

For Go repositories, map modules, build tags, entry points, migrations, credentials, authorization, concurrency, startup/daemon lifecycle, and output contracts before changing code. Prefer surgical fixes with focused tests, race verification where relevant, and cross-platform checks for filesystem, shell, and process behavior.

### Python engineering

For Python repositories, preserve deterministic environments and provenance. Pin vendored inputs to commits, record manifests, isolate platform-specific behavior, and run targeted tests plus the smallest meaningful integration or cross-platform matrix before broad validation.

### Web application engineering

For React, SvelteKit, Vite, Cloudflare/OpenNext, and offline-first applications, treat runtime routing, browser behavior, deployment configuration, caching, service workers, and visual quality as separate contracts. Verify production-like builds and exact external routes, not only internal health checks; preserve rollback artifacts for deployment changes.

### Editor and Zed engineering

For editor work, distinguish configuration/theme portability from editor-runtime internals. Declarative theme conversion must preserve semantic scopes and be assertion-checked; typography requires checking font-family collisions, weight resolution, and UI-font limitations. For Zed/Rust/GPUI/WASM changes, respect WIT host/guest versioning, entity lifecycles, panel/dock/status-bar wiring, and bounded per-crate verification. Treat embedded-font extraction and binary inspection as evidence-producing steps, not guesswork.

## Verification and handoff

Record the files changed, commands run, test scope, known gaps, and rollback path. For release or deployment changes, verify artifact identity and the actual running route/version independently. Keep narrow provider- or editor-specific notes in the absorbed references rather than duplicating them in this umbrella.

## Reference map

Use the absorbed `references/` files for detailed workflows rather than expanding this umbrella with session-specific recipes. GitHub/worktree/review material is under `references/git-surgical-operations.md`, `references/worktree-impl-and-review.md`, `references/pr-conflicts-and-merge.md`, and the dependency-verification references. Go-specific evidence is under `references/go-repository-mapping-and-audit.md` and the adjacent Go correctness notes. Python and cross-platform subprocess guidance is under `references/cross-platform-subprocess-review.md`, `references/pydantic-ai-harness.md`, and `references/cliniar-cli-and-linear-backend.md`.

## Neighboring boundary

This umbrella owns general software engineering and delivery: repository change
method, Go/Python/web implementation, editor and Zed internals, and the
Git/worktree/GitHub/PR/release lifecycle. It absorbed six former standalone
skills — `go-build-and-surgical-fixes`,
`python-cross-platform-change-and-test`, `web-application-product-engineering`,

## Commit early to survive silent working-tree wipes

Two independently observed incident classes destroy uncommitted work with no
tool error and no visible cause in the transcript: (1) a probe/adversarial
agent running `git checkout -- <file>` believing it "reverts a probe change"
(see references/restore-lost-uncommitted-wiring.md), and (2) an unattributed
automatic `git reset --hard HEAD` between ordinary tool calls with no agent-
issued destructive git command anywhere in the transcript (confirmed via
`git reflog` showing a bare `reset: moving to HEAD` entry) — filed as
Swarm-Code/mono#327. In both cases `git status`/`git diff` silently go clean;
there is no error to catch.

Mitigation: once a multi-file edit for one fix is applied AND verified
(`go build`/`go test` scoped to the right module passes), `git add` + commit
it immediately before starting the next investigation or edit — do not batch
several verified fixes into one pending, uncommitted working tree. A commit
is durable against this failure class; an uncommitted `apply_patch` result is
not, no matter how many tool results confirmed it landed. If a wipe is
suspected mid-task (unexpectedly empty `git status` after prior successful
edits), check `git reflog` for an unexplained `reset:` entry before assuming
you imagined the earlier edits, and report it via `annoyed` as a harness
defect (category tool_failure) rather than silently redoing the work without
flagging it.



## CRITICAL: when working in a dedicated git worktree, Bash's own `cd` does NOT default there — verify every single shell invocation targets the worktree, not the primary checkout

Confirmed 2026-08-13 in `Swarm-Code/mono`. When a task assigns a dedicated worktree (e.g.
`/home/swarm/Work/mono/.worktrees/<name>` on branch `fix/<name>`), `apply_patch` calls correctly
resolve against that worktree (its cwd default is the session workspace root, which the harness
pins to the worktree). But **`Bash` calls do NOT inherit that same default** — a `cd
/home/swarm/Work/mono/swarm-sdk && go build/test ...` command silently operates on the **primary
checkout** (typically on `main` or whatever branch it happens to be on), a completely different,
unmodified copy of the repo, if you type the path without the `.worktrees/<name>/` prefix.

Symptom that exposed this: `apply_patch` reported "Success" and added new `_test.go` functions;
`go vet`/`go build` from `cd .../mono/swarm-sdk` also reported success with zero errors; but
`go test -run <new test names>` printed **"no tests to run"** and `go test -list` didn't list the
new functions at all — because the primary checkout never received the edits, so vet/build/test
were all silently validating stale, pre-patch code. Nothing in the tool output flagged this: no
error, no path mismatch warning, just quietly-wrong results that looked like a real test-discovery
failure until `git status --short` was run from BOTH directories and compared.

**Mandatory habit for any worktree-scoped task**: after the first `apply_patch`, immediately run
`git status --short <path>` from the exact worktree directory you intend to build/test in and
confirm the edited files show as modified there — do not assume path-typing consistency is enough.
If a `Bash` command's `cd` target does not literally start with the worktree's assigned path
prefix (check it against the task's `--workspace` value / the conversation's stated worktree path),
treat every prior build/test result run under the wrong path as invalid and rerun from the correct
one before trusting green output. This is the `Bash`-tool analogue of the already-documented
`apply_patch`-lands-in-wrong-repo family of gotchas (see `clover-platform-operations`'s TILs on
`apply_patch` and git worktrees) — the direction is reversed here (edits land correctly, but
*verification* silently targets the wrong copy) but the root discipline is the same: always
`git status --short` the exact directory you are about to trust a build/test result from.
